There is also an analogy in the names of other festivals, τ. ἐγκαίνια, ἄζυμα, etc.): , ; ἡ ἡμέρα τῶν σ. (Ex 20:8, al.), , ; dat. pl. G4561.as:
σάρξ, σαρκός, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for בָּשָׂר ;]

1. as in cl. generally,
(a) prop., of the soft substance of the animal body: , , , al.; σ. καὶ αἷμα, ; σ. καὶ ὀστέα, ; pl., of the flesh of many or parts of the flesh of one (cl.), ; φαγεῖν, Re, ll. c. (cf. κατεσθίειν, IV Ki 9:36, al., and βιβρώσκειν, freq. in l.); metaph., ; mystically, φ. (τρώγειν) τὴν σ. τοῦ υἱοῦ τ. ἀνθρώπου, ;
(b) Of the whole substance of the body, = σῶμα: (LXX), , , , ; μία σ., ; εἰς σ. μίαν (Ge 2:24), , , , ; hence, of the material as opp. to the immaterial part of man (cf. Lft., Notes, 88): opp. to πνεῦμα, , , , , ; to ψύχη, , Rec.; of the present life, ἐν (τῇ) σ., , , , ; of Christ's life on earth, αἱ ἡμέραι τ. σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ, ; of things pertaining to the body, ἐν (τῇ) σ., , , , .
2. As in Heb. idiom,
(a) of a living creature: πᾶσα σ. (Heb. כָּל־בָּשָׂר; cf. Bl., § 47, 9), , , ; esp. of man and his mortality (Ps 55 (56):5, Si 28:5, al.), ; πᾶσα σ. (v. supr.), , , , ἐν σ., , ;
(b) of natural origin and relationship (Ge 2:24, Is 58:7, al.): τέκνα τῆς σ., ; κατὰ σάρκα, , , , , ; ἡ σ. μου, (cf. Jg 9:2, II Ki 5:1, al.).
3. Of the physical nature as subject to sensation and desire (Plut.),
(a) without any ethical disparagement: ; opp. to πνεῦμα, , ; τ. θέλημα τῆς σ., ; ἡ ἐπιθυμία τῆς σ., ; pl., ; παθεῖν σαρκί, ;
(b) in ethical sense, esp. in Pauline Epp., of the flesh as the seat and vehicle of sinful desires: opp. to νοῦς, ; to πνεῦμα, , , , , , (cf. DB, ii, 14f.; iv, 165f.; Cremer, 844 ff.).
